records.text:
Hi and welcome to the Lenovo Community
Vechtrul
,
I understand your queries about the Screen Protection feature on your Lenovo Legion Pro 32UD-10 monitor. And great job being proactive about OLED care.
Based on how OLED maintenance features are designed on the 32UD-10:
Automatic “Screen Protection”
(every ~4 hours): When you accept the prompt, it runs a short compensation/pixel refresh cycle. This typically completes in about 1–2 minutes and is intended to clear minor image retention from recent use.
Manual “Panel Protect” (OSD): This initiates a full (deep) compensation cycle, which takes longer—around 5 minutes—and performs a more thorough recalibration of the panel. It’s safe to use, but not necessary to run frequently unless you notice persistent image retention.
If you miss the screen-protection prompt: The monitor will
defer the short cycle and typically perform it the next time the monitor is idle/enters
standby or is powered off normally. To ensure it can complete, avoid cutting power at the wall immediately—let the monitor go to sleep or power off via the button/OS so it can run any scheduled maintenance.
What’s recommended: For most users, leave the automatic protection enabled and let the monitor manage the short cycles. Use Panel Protect occasionally (e.g., if you notice retention that doesn’t clear after regular use or after an automatic cycle). Running the deep cycle too often won’t harm the panel, but it’s unnecessary for routine care.
Additional OLED care tips: - Enable features like Pixel Shift and Logo Dimming/Screen Saver in the OSD to reduce static element retention. - Vary on-screen content and avoid long periods of static UI elements at high brightness.
Hope this helps you out. Please let us know if you have any other concerns or queries.
Best regards,
Adriel_Lenovo

records.text:
Hi and welcome to the Lenovo Community
Metasotku
,
I understand your question on if what HDR mode will give 1000 nit full brightness on the Lenovo Legion Pro 32UD-10 monitor.
To address your concern:
• Peak brightness: The advertised 1000‑nit level is reached only during HDR playback with appropriate scene content (small bright highlights) and with local dimming active. The specific HDR preset that consistently drives full peak luminance can vary by content and settings; please refer to the monitor’s PSREF/spec sheet for the official brightness spec and supported HDR formats: Lenovo Product Specifications Reference (PSREF) by clicking
here
.
• Oversaturated colors in HDR Photo/Movie/Gaming: Those presets are tuned for a more vivid look and can oversaturate compared to accurate HDR tone mapping. To reduce oversaturation: - In the monitor OSD, switch from the HDR “Photo/Movie/Gaming” presets to a more neutral/standard HDR mode if available, or select a user/custom mode and set Color Gamut to Auto or sRGB. - Disable any image enhancement features (e.g., dynamic contrast, vivid/color boost) within the OSD when using HDR. - Ensure the GPU output is set to full-range and high bit depth (e.g., RGB Full, 10‑bit where supported) in your graphics control panel. - Re‑enable local dimming for correct HDR contrast. - Calibrate HDR in the OS (Windows HDR settings and calibration) and confirm your content is HDR10.
• Firmware/updates: If the OSD does not provide a neutral HDR preset or you still see over‑saturation after the steps above, check for the latest monitor firmware/driver on the Lenovo Support site via this other
link
.
Hope this helps.
Thanks,
Adriel_Lenovo

records.author: Adriel_lenovo
records.text:
Hi and welcome to the Lenovo Community
Kyletsit
,
I'm sorry to know that you're having difficulties setting up the refresh rate on your Lenovo Legion Pro 27Q-10 monitor. Based on your description, what you’re seeing is consistent with bandwidth and signaling limits by interface and settings. 2560×1440 at very high refresh and 10-bit color can exceed uncompressed HDMI bandwidth on some monitor/GPU combos, so DSC and/or reduced color depth/chroma may be required. On this model, 280 Hz is typically achieved over DisplayPort with DSC, while HDMI may present lower maximum modes depending on color format and firmware.
Please try the following:
1) Update firmware/drivers - Monitor: Check for a monitor firmware and driver/INF on the Lenovo support site by clicking
here
. - GPU: Update to the latest AMD Adrenalin driver for your RX 7800 XT. - OS: Ensure Windows 11 is current. For Linux, update kernel/Mesa to the latest stable versions.
2) Verify OSD settings on the monitor - HDMI Version/Compatibility: In the monitor OSD, make sure the HDMI input is set to “HDMI 2.1” (FRL) and not a compatibility/1.4 mode. - DSC: If there is an HDMI DSC toggle in the OSD, test with it enabled first. Then test disabled to compare. - Overclock: Ensure any “Overclock/280 Hz” setting is enabled for DP (you’ve confirmed DP reaches 280 Hz with DSC). Note: Some overclock settings apply to DP only.
3) Windows display and AMD settings (HDMI tests) - Windows > Settings > System > Display > Advanced display: Set 2560×1440 and test 8-bit first to see higher refresh rate options appear. Then try 10-bit. - AMD Adrenalin > Settings > Display: - Toggle “Display Stream Compression (DSC)” on for the HDMI display and retest (some drivers expose this per display). - Change Pixel Format to YCbCr 4:2:2 or 4:2:0 to see if higher refresh rates become available, then move back to RGB/10-bit if desired. - Try another certified “Ultra High Speed HDMI” cable if available to rule out cable signaling issues.
4) Linux notes (HDMI tests) - Ensure amdgpu DC is enabled and DSC support is present (kernel 6.x+ and recent Mesa). - Use your DE’s display settings or xrandr to enumerate modes; some environments may default to conservative modes.
5) Check interface-specific limits - Some monitors advertise different maximum refresh rates by interface and color format. Please refer to the Product Specifications in its Lenovo Product Specifications Reference (PSREF) for the
Legion Pro 27Q-10
to confirm the maximum refresh supported over HDMI versus DisplayPort, and whether DSC and/or reduced chroma/bit depth is required for high-refresh modes. - If PSREF indicates that HDMI is limited to lower refresh at 1440p (especially at 10-bit RGB), then what you’re seeing would be expected behavior. In that case, DisplayPort remains the recommended path for 280 Hz.
About the missing power cable - The monitor package should include a power cord. We’re sorry yours wasn’t in the box. Since you had a spare, you’re up and running, but we can still help with the missing accessory: - If recently purchased, contact your retailer to report the missing item. - You can also check part availability via
Lenovo Parts Lookup page
or submit a request with the technical support using
Service Request
for assistance.
Hope this helps.
Thanks,
Adriel_Lenovo
